description: Lutetium is a silvery white metal with atomic number 71, classified as the last element in the lanthanide series and also as the first element of the sixth-period transition metals. It resists corrosion in dry air but not in moist air. Lutetium is the smallest lanthanide atom due to lanthanide contraction, and it has the highest density, melting point, and hardness among the lanthanides.
uses: Lutetium-176 is used to determine the age of minerals and meteorites. 177Lu-DOTA-TATE is used for radionuclide therapy on neuroendocrine tumours. Stable lutetium can be used as catalysts in petroleum cracking and in alkylation, hydrogenation, and polymerization applications. Lutetium compounds are used in high refractive index immersion lithography and as dopants in gadolinium gallium garnet for magnetic bubble memory devices, as well as in positron emission tomography detectors.
characteristics: Lutetium is a silvery white metal that burns readily at 150°C to form lutetium oxide. It has the highest Brinell hardness of any lanthanide at 890–1300 MPa and the highest density and melting point among lanthanides. Lutetium generally exists in the +3 oxidation state and its compounds form colorless aqueous solutions that typically produce white crystalline solids, except for the brown iodide.
